title: VHELM: A Holistic Evaluation of Vision Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models using the PAIRS dataset with image pairs differing only by gender to test for stereotypical associations in occupation, status, or potential crime, and measuring performance disparities in facial attribute recognition across genders using the FairFace dataset.

Probing models with the PAIRS dataset using images of individuals differing only by race (White vs. Black) to check for unwarranted associations, and measuring VQA performance disparities across seven distinct racial groups using the FairFace dataset.
Measuring performance disparities in visual question answering (e.g., predicting age groups) across different age demographics using the FairFace dataset.
Assessing performance disparity by comparing captioning and VQA accuracy on images sourced from diverse geographical regions worldwide using the Crossmodal-3600 and Bingo (Region Bias) datasets.

Testing counterfactual fairness by introducing African-American English (AAE) perturbations into standard English prompts (in VQAv2 and A-OKVQA datasets) to measure the impact of linguistic diversity on model performance.
